phase: Phase S3: Structured output for the evaluation features
summary: Two S3 contract failures block acceptance. Structured SDK debug logging exposes the key and text. The BM2 chatbot strip drops lesson math.
blocking_findings: ADV-S3-5 [Blocker] adversarial-testing: packages/ai-tutoring/src/lesson-context.ts:69 consumes the newline after an empty detail label. The tutor receives only the second math sentence. The accepted limit in evidence.md:361-364 covers math on the label line only. Failing test: ADV-S3-5: keeps the first math sentence on the line after an empty detail label.

ADV-S3-8 [Blocker] adversarial-testing: packages/ai-tutoring/src/structured.ts:150-153 supplies no safe logger. With OPENROUTER_DEBUG=1, the installed SDK prints the authorization key, prompt, and answer. The structured result still succeeds. Failing test: ADV-S3-8: structured SDK debug output omits the key, prompt, and answer.
evidence: Slot check passed. Git confirmed that b0bb87d4 was the role base and that 55e7952b was its ancestor. Reviews A, B, and C passed on that HEAD.
ADV-S3-1 and ADV-S3-7: the installed SDK sends the exact schema name, strict setting, generated schema, and provider object. The SDK receives a mocked fetch response only.

ADV-S3-2: wire cases preserve invalid_json and schema_mismatch. The disconnect probe retries and returns the next valid answer. Original tests cover HTTP retry, empty content, abort, and spreadsheet transport errors.

ADV-S3-2 and ADV-S3-3: the real teacher route returns the same five response keys and the deterministic summary for a schema mismatch and HTTP 400. The user message contains the lesson and no fixture details. The response keeps the name and email.
ADV-S3-4: the original BM2 route test exercises the shared assembler. It omits all six fixture values and keeps both math sentences. All eight IM3 PII cases pass.
ADV-S3-5: the BM2 route returns 200 and sends one provider request. Its system prompt keeps the check sentence but drops the equation sentence.
ADV-S3-6: wire scores -1 and 41 become 0 and 40. Each list keeps its first three items. A non-string fourth item triggers deterministic feedback.

ADV-S3-8: providers.ts:464 derives a cache key from role and model. Existing tests cover key rotation and removal. The existing chat debug guard passes, but the structured log test finds the key, prompt, and answer.
ADV-S3-9: the installed SDK returns a bare key as the served model. The model field is null in the usage record, and a :free suffix remains valid.
ADV-S3-10: two warmed multi-message providers send the correct model and message under concurrent requests.
Red comparison: at 36b27a50 the wire preference is empty and the served model is a key. Both assertions pass at b0bb87d4. The structured debug failure persists on both trees.

The committed logs red-s3-cc7bb7b4.log and red-s3-fix-ff30c052.log record the original Red cases. The main Red tree lacks the new helper and teacher generator, so it cannot execute every added wire probe.
A4 rejects two in-progress tasks. A7 preserves both diagnostic lines with exclusion words. The S3 plan has no literal A5 all-pass claim.
The brief identifies the open S3 manual verification task as PM-verified. It is not a finding.
The build graph returns no callers for three queried symbols. The exact phase diff and source imports identify the paths the tests use.
Commit b39b1c57a5da463508eff64e7b25b9a00e90382a changes five test files only and has a Git note. No generated or graph file is staged.

The two failed tests carry expected-red comments and run as normal tests. Both failures qualify for the late wrong-result exception. The round limit still applies after the two S3 remediation commits 9352efac and 43f08c9d.
adv-s3-b0bb87d4-failure-keys.log shows that the gate key function preserves the exact two adversarial failure titles.
The full S3 sweep reports NEWFAIL=1. Compared with s2, the only new Vitest failure titles are ADV-S3-5 and ADV-S3-8. See adv-s3-b0bb87d4-sweep-keys.log.
